# HopCLI

> hop is a fast, atomic package manager for the terminal: parallel installs, instant rollback (a single symlink swap, no re-download), a content-addressed store where nothing is ever edited in place, and zero runtime dependencies (one static Go binary). It competes directly with Homebrew and can pull nearly 200 of Homebrew's own formulae straight from ghcr.io/homebrew/core, relocated to run from hop's own store.

Every install, upgrade, or removal is one transaction: hop downloads and verifies every artifact first, then flips a single symlink to activate the new state. If anything fails partway through, nothing changes — the previous state stays live. `hop rollback` reverses any change instantly because every earlier version is still on disk, untouched.

## Pages

- [Home](https://hopcli-site.onrender.com/): what hop is, why it exists, how it compares to Homebrew, install instructions.
- [Docs](https://hopcli-site.onrender.com/docs.html): hub linking the pages below.
- [Commands](https://hopcli-site.onrender.com/commands.html): every hop command (install, upgrade, rollback, alias, migrate, self-update, and the rest) with usage and flags, transcribed directly from the CLI's own help output.
- [Architecture](https://hopcli-site.onrender.com/architecture.html): how the content-addressed store, generations, and atomic transactions actually work.
- [Homebrew relocation](https://hopcli-site.onrender.com/relocation.html): how hop rewrites a Homebrew bottle (built for a fixed system path) to run from hop's own arbitrary store location — placeholder tokens, RPATH/LC_RPATH patching, and the real bugs it took to get right.
- [Migrating from Homebrew](https://hopcli-site.onrender.com/migrate.html): a full walkthrough of `hop migrate`.
- [Changelog](https://hopcli-site.onrender.com/changelog.html): what changed in each tagged release.
